Unresolved question: What is the intended operational boundary and who is the railway authority for this system?
Why it matters: Determines whether this is an offline planning aid, a dispatch-connected system, or an authorized operational workflow; authority and assurance requirements differ.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Offline prototype only: no operational release claim and use clearly labeled non-authoritative data. B. Planning support: define human approval and authoritative interfaces. C. Operational control: requires authority-led safety lifecycle and integration scope beyond current prototype.
Implementation blocked until resolved: Yes for any operational implementation or safety claim

Unresolved question: Which infrastructure registry and version define segments, sections, lines, directions, routes, and assets?
Why it matters: Current code creates corridor sections proportionally and uses two line enums; incorrect mapping affects every conflict calculation.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Adopt an existing authoritative registry: integrate versioned IDs and mapping. B. Build/maintain a governed topology source: assign ownership and validation. C. No source available: block topology-dependent operational claims.

Unresolved question: How are logical adjacency, shared assets, junctions, crossovers, and conflict groups defined?
Why it matters: Logical adjacency cannot be inferred solely from physical distance, section labels, or line names.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Explicit versioned adjacency graph: supports relationship-based rules. B. Activity-specific conflict matrix over assets: more precise but needs ownership. C. Conservative blanket conflict: may over-block and still needs scope approval.

Unresolved question: What geometry/chainage reference, accuracy, uncertainty and conversion defines a worksite and train footprint?
Why it matters: Spatial clearance depends on a common calibrated coordinate basis and actual extents.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Authoritative chainage registry with accuracy bounds. B. Geospatial coordinates with approved CRS and transformation. C. Insufficient geometry: spatial check remains UNKNOWN; no distance-based pass.

Unresolved question: What buffer, equipment envelope, measurement method, boundary equality, and uncertainty policy apply to each work/activity combination?
Why it matters: Current verifier hardcodes 1,000 m, 2,000 m, and 1,000 m adjacent buffers without approved source; adopting them would silently turn prototype constants into policy.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Owner-approved activity/equipment-specific parameters. B. Rule-based values supplied by an authorized external safety system. C. No approved value: keep check unresolved and prevent verified status.

Unresolved question: Which timetable/movement provider is authoritative for each route, operating date, and movement class?
Why it matters: The bundled CSV and custom uploads are not shown to be authenticated or complete; missing trains can make modeled time look free.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Authenticated operational feed with a named provider. B. Governed timetable database with signed export/version. C. None available: only non-authoritative candidate generation; status remains unverified.

Unresolved question: What exactly constitutes complete timetable coverage and how is freshness established?
Why it matters: A list of movements and a caller-supplied source name do not prove completeness; verification needs a defined negative-occupancy basis.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Signed coverage attestation scoped by date, time, route, line, section and version. B. Independently reconciled provider completeness protocol. C. No evidence: UNKNOWN; never pass absence-of-train check.

Unresolved question: What operating-date, time-zone, service-day, overnight, and clock-change semantics apply?
Why it matters: Current intervals are floating hour-of-day values; the dataset has days_of_week but the data engine does not use it to create date-specific windows.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Store absolute instants plus named zone and service calendar. B. Use railway-defined operating-day convention with explicit mapping. C. No approved semantics: reject date-ambiguous inputs.

Unresolved question: How are cancellations, delays, diversions, unscheduled trains, missed updates, and feed corrections represented and propagated?
Why it matters: An initially valid schedule may become invalid after timetable changes.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Ordered update stream with sequence and revocation. B. Poll/version refresh plus explicit revalidation before use. C. No lifecycle integration: expire schedule/evidence and require manual review; no continued verification.

Unresolved question: What work activities require a possession, closure, movement restriction, or other operational authority, and who grants it?
Why it matters: A planned maintenance interval is not a granted possession or track closure.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Activity-class policy maps to authenticated authority grants. B. External operations workflow supplies per-job approval. C. No authority integration: solver result remains a proposal and cannot be treated as released.

Unresolved question: What traction/electrical assets, isolation scope, state and authorized confirmation source apply to each job?
Why it matters: A Boolean `power_isolated` or source label cannot establish electrical isolation; work may depend on exact circuits and intervals.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Authenticated provider/permit record bound to asset, worksite, date, interval, actor and validity. B. Approved human workflow with verifiable record. C. No source: UNKNOWN and no verified traction work.

Unresolved question: What worksite-protection arrangements and evidence are required for each task class?
Why it matters: The project does not define or model worksite protection; inventing procedures would be unsafe and outside software evidence.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Authority-owned rule catalogue and authenticated approval. B. External protection-plan system provides scoped record. C. Undefined: block safety verification for affected tasks.

Unresolved question: Which maintenance task taxonomy maps work types to qualifications, equipment, possession/isolation needs, and conflict rules?
Why it matters: Current defect_type is free text and department enum is not a task eligibility or qualification model.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Controlled versioned catalogue maintained by maintenance authority. B. Refer to an authoritative work-order platform. C. No validated mapping: reject unknown tasks or leave requirements UNKNOWN.

Unresolved question: How should maintenance priority trade against aggregate work-order coverage?
Why it matters: Current urgency influences search ordering, not a binding optimized priority; lexicographic priority can select different work than maximum count.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Priority-tier lexicographic coverage before total count. B. Total count first, then priority tie-break. C. Owner-defined service classes/deadlines. Each produces different selected work; no choice is implied here.

Unresolved question: What lexicographic order should disruption, schedule stability, workload balance, utilization, and co-location follow after hard feasibility and coverage?
Why it matters: Current baseline and CP-SAT use combined/scaled terms; priorities may conflict and weights are not domain-approved.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Owner-approved lexicographic tiers. B. Pareto alternatives shown to planner for approval. C. Approved weighted objective with documented units and sensitivity analysis. No weighting is assumed.

Unresolved question: How is train/service disruption measured and which movements/services may be affected?
Why it matters: Current objective uses local time-of-day and a two-hour train-gap heuristic, not validated delay or service impact.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Authority-defined impact model using movement/priority data. B. External operations cost metric. C. No model: omit disruption claims and report only solver-side proxy clearly labeled.

Unresolved question: Which crew pools, credentials, validity rules, availability, capacity and historical duty data may be used?
Why it matters: Department labels do not establish qualified or available staff; no crew data exists in the project.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Integrate authoritative crew/credential systems. B. Planner-provided validated roster with explicit completeness/freshness. C. No data: cannot claim crew-feasible schedule.

Unresolved question: What equipment types, quantities, capacities, compatibility, maintenance state and movement envelopes apply?
Why it matters: A heavy-equipment Boolean neither identifies a machine nor constrains its simultaneous use.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Equipment asset registry plus reservation calendars. B. Validated planner assignments and compatibility rules. C. No inventory: no equipment-feasibility claim; unknown affected checks.

Unresolved question: What travel, access, mobilization, setup, dismantling, and transition-time model is approved?
Why it matters: Nonoverlapping assignments can still be impossible for one resource to execute sequentially.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Versioned route/network model with resource-specific travel. B. Conservative approved transition table. C. No reliable transition data: do not assign shared resources across sites as feasible.
Implementation blocked until resolved: Yes where resources move between jobs

Unresolved question: Which shift, duty, break, maximum-work and rest policies apply, with what rolling horizon and history?
Why it matters: Current 8-hour bins are workload accounting only and cannot be treated as working-time rules.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Authority-approved policy engine. B. External crew schedule supplies allowed intervals. C. No policy/history: mark resource feasibility unknown.

Unresolved question: How are work durations estimated, including uncertainty, setup, contingency, phases, interruptions, and restart costs?
Why it matters: Current generator creates fixed durations; solver models one continuous fixed interval.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Approved fixed duration plus conservative margin. B. Duration distribution/robust or scenario planning. C. Phase/splittable task model. Each changes feasibility and needs planner evidence.

Unresolved question: Which earliest starts, latest completions, hard deadlines, preferred windows, and calendar exceptions apply per work order?
Why it matters: No such fields exist; urgency cannot substitute for a deadline.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Authoritative work-order date windows. B. Operations possession windows. C. No input: reject tasks whose window is required or mark that constraint unknown.
Implementation blocked until resolved: Yes for tasks with binding windows/deadlines

Unresolved question: What dependency types, lag, predecessor state, waiver authority, and cycle semantics apply?
Why it matters: No dependency data exists; omitting precedence can produce invalid sequences.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Explicit DAG with owner-approved lag. B. External workflow state machine. C. No reliable dependency data: block affected tasks or mark unknown.

Unresolved question: When may tasks co-locate, and what shared access, crew, equipment, possession and protection conditions are required?
Why it matters: Current exact-window bilateral Boolean is a prototype exception and can create overlaps not justified by shared-site evidence.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Controlled pair/task compatibility catalogue plus resource checks. B. Disallow co-location until explicitly approved per job. C. Permit only via authenticated joint-work approval. Outcomes differ; current Boolean is not sufficient.

Unresolved question: What solver outcome, proof state, partial output, unscheduled reason, and API-status semantics are canonical?
Why it matters: Baseline and CP-SAT use different partial/unschedulable labels; cutoff, feasibility, maximum coverage and objective proof are distinct.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Separate coverage state, termination reason and proof flags. B. Single outcome enum plus documented precedence and metadata. Must not infer unschedulability from a limit or per-order cause from global proof.
Implementation blocked until resolved: Yes before solver integration or operator use

Unresolved question: What evidence states, applicability rules, audit denominator, retention, and revocation behavior are required?
Why it matters: Current audit uses bool/null and represents some not-applicable rules as passed; percentages can be misunderstood if denominator is unclear.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Explicit PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN/NOT_APPLICABLE states and applicable-only denominator. B. Existing bool/null contract with rigorously specified N/A marker and denominator. No empty/incomplete audit may establish verification.

Unresolved question: What data retention, privacy, security, access control, and auditability apply to work, timetable, crew, and safety evidence?
Why it matters: Future authoritative records may be sensitive and need governed access and nonrepudiable provenance.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Existing railway data governance policy. B. New project-specific policy approved before integration. C. No policy: do not ingest or persist sensitive operational/credential data.

Unresolved question: What schedule-change events invalidate a prior result, and who can re-authorize it?
Why it matters: The current prototype has no lifecycle/version invalidation; a stale plan may appear current after data changes.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Invalidate on any relevant source-version change and re-run all checks. B. Rule-based impact analysis with human review for affected scope. C. No reliable change feed: expire all outputs after approved validity interval.
Implementation blocked until resolved: Yes before schedule reuse or release

Unresolved question: Which proof requirements must be met before presenting an objective as optimal or coverage as maximum?
Why it matters: Baseline exposes no global objective proof; CP-SAT proves only its encoded model and may stop with a feasible incumbent.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Expose separate coverage/objective proof flags. B. Report only incumbent and bound/gap when solver provides them. C. Do not claim optimality if no proof or meaningful bound.

Unresolved question: Which representative, governed datasets and workload distributions may be used for future benchmark and validation?
Why it matters: Task 12 is synthetic with shared timetable windows and sizes 10/25/50; the generator contains 90 work orders.
Available alternatives and consequences: A. Authorized de-identified historic/representative dataset with coverage metadata. B. Approved scenario generator calibrated by domain owners and clearly synthetic. C. No representative data: limit conclusions to prototype benchmark only.
